@graph.headline: The Flat Rate Movers publish their dataset estate with a citable DOI

acceptedAnswer.text: The estate's dataset collection — the dataset files behind the website, both entity graphs, the signed master index, and the 53-area service footprint — deposited at Zenodo as a citable dataset; Wikidata entries for the company, the owner's book, and the dataset; both branch listings on OpenStreetMap; the two Hugging Face mirrors brought current; and a Google Publisher Center publication. Each record lives on its own platform and can be opened and checked there.

mainEntity.name: What exactly did the company publish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cite the concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23879048. A concept DOI always resolves to the latest version of the deposit, so a citation stays current as the record is versioned. The deposit is credited to Pitts, Henry, published by The Flat Rate Movers, and licensed CC BY 4.0.

mainEntity.name: How do I cite the dataset?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The Zenodo deposit is published under CC BY 4.0, which permits reuse with attribution, and the Hugging Face mirrors carry the same license. The signed master index exists so a reuser can check that a file is the company's file and unchanged — the digest of every distribution is in the index, and the index itself is signed.

No. The company runs the same 30 services from the same two branches, priced the same way it has priced work since June 2010: the full scope reviewed, then one flat rate in writing, hourly pricing is available when a client asks for it. The publication is a record of the company as it operates — it is not a new service, a new price, or a new claim.
